origin.description: This function creates colors of class HLS; a subclass of the virtual color class.

arguments.name: H, L, S
arguments.text: Hue, lightness, and saturation. Separate vectors or a three-column matrix passed as H.

arguments.name: names
arguments.text: Row names for the colors. By default the row names of H are used.

origin.details: Hues should lie between 0 and 360; lightness and saturation between 0 and 1. HLS is a relative color space derived from RGB. Conversion to another space goes through a specific RGB space such as sRGB.
origin.value: An object of class HLS which inherits from class color. The coords slot is a matrix with columns H, L, and S.

translation.description: This function creates colors of class HLS; a subclass of the virtual color class.

arguments.name: H, L, S
arguments.text: Hue, lightness, and saturation as separate arrays or scalars, or an n by 3 matrix as H when L and S are omitted. Scalars for L or S recycle to the length of H.

arguments.name: names
arguments.text: Row names. When H is a (matrix, rownames) pair, row names default from the pair if names is omitted.

translation.details: Hues should lie between 0 and 360; lightness and saturation between 0 and 1. Calling HLS() with no H returns an empty HLS object. A matrix that is not n by 3, or a length mismatch after recycling, raises invalid color matrix.
translation.value: An HLSColor object. space is HLS, coords is an n by 3 float64 array with columns H, L, and S, and names is the row names or None.
translation.example:
from colorspace.hls import HLS
import numpy as np

print(HLS(np.linspace(0, 360, 13)[:-1], 0.5, 1))
